title: Cocycle of the canonical fixed-point stalk transports
statement:
Use the global finite-field and finite-coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k$ its fixed algebraic closure, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ with $n\geq1$ and $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, $X_0$ separated of finite type over $k_0$, $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$. Let $\Phi:X\to X$ be the $k$-linear $q$-power scheme Frobenius and $g=g_\gamma$ the geometric Galois-Frobenius automorphism [def-trf-scheme-frobenius]. Use the derived module pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and put $Q_j=L(\Phi^j)^*$ and $P_j=L(g^j)^*$ for $j\geq1$. Fix a $k$-morphism $z:s\to X$ and a positive integer $d$ with $\Phi^d z=z$. Write $J_z(L)=L_z=R\Gamma(s_{\mathrm{proet}},Lz^*L)$ for the ordinary derived geometric stalk [pur9-def-derived-stalk], for $L\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$.

For each positive multiple $j$ of $d$, let $\rho_{j,L}:J_z(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_z(Q_jL)$ be the canonical composition comparison $L(\Phi^jz)^*\cong Lz^*Q_j$, followed by derived sections, with its source identified using $\Phi^jz=z$. The composition comparisons are those of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], with canonical constant-coefficient identifications. Using the specified multiplicative natural isomorphism $\kappa^{(j)}:Q_j\xrightarrow{\sim}P_j$ of [prop-trf-scheme-galois-comparison], put
$$t_{j,L}=J_z(\kappa^{(j)}_L)\circ\rho_{j,L}:J_z(L)\xrightarrow{\sim}J_z(P_jL).$$
Then $t_j$ is natural in $L$: for every morphism $u:L\to M$,
$$J_z(P_j u)\circ t_{j,L}=t_{j,M}\circ J_z(u).$$
For positive multiples $a,b$ of $d$, let $c_{a,b}:P_{a+b}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_aP_b$ be the canonical pullback-composition comparison (using $g^{a+b}=g^b\circ g^a$). Then
$$J_z(c_{a,b,L})\circ t_{a+b,L}=t_{a,P_bL}\circ t_{b,L}.$$
No Weil structure on $L$, closed point below $z$, trace, or perfectness hypothesis is assumed.
